notes:
CIRCUIT: five inverting op-amp stages (all four op-amps have their in+ tied to a GND symbol and a reactive/resistive feedback element from output back to in-), fed by a 5V source (top left) and a 10A current source (lower left), with the three right-hand output resistors (#6, #13, #22) all landing on one common vertical bus at x~986. 24 components, 12 nets.

NET MAP:
  0   = ground: in+ of every op-amp (2.0, 10.0, 14.0, 20.0), GND symbols #7 #8 #15 #17 #19 #23, bottom lead of V-DC #5, bottom lead of I-DC #16.
  n1  = output node of op-amp #2: OA2 out (2.2), RIGHT plate of cap #0, LEFT lead of resistor #4. Physically the blob at (414,210), the wire up x~414 to y~100 and left to the cap's right plate, and the (faded) run right along y~208 to the 1k resistor at x~487.
  n2  = summing node (in-) of op-amp #3: OA3 t1 (upper-left lead at (641,205)), RIGHT lead of resistor #4, LEFT lead of inductor #1 (the 1uH feedback). Physically the y~205 wire from x~555 to the op-amp, plus the x~600 drop from the inductor (site S4).
  n3  = output node of op-amp #3: OA3 out (747,234), RIGHT lead of inductor #1, LEFT lead of resistor #6. The x~752 riser (site S10) carries the inductor feedback.
  n4  = summing node (in-) of op-amp #2: OA2 t1 (upper-left lead at (279,192)), TOP terminal of V-DC #5, LEFT plate of cap #0. Physically the y~197 rail from x=62 to x=280 plus the x~185 riser to the y~93 top rail.
  n5  = the shared middle node: in+ of op-amp #3 (3.0), RIGHT lead of inductor #11, LEFT lead of resistor #12, OUTPUT of op-amp #14 (14.2), LEFT plate of cap #21. Physically the y~500 rail from x~260 to x~555, the staircase up (439,500)->(487,383)->(580,320)->(600,250)->OA3 in+, and the drop from (439,500) to y~822 then right to cap #21.
  n6  = the right-hand output bus at x~986: RIGHT lead of resistor #6, RIGHT lead of resistor #13, RIGHT lead of resistor #22.
  n7  = summing node (in-) of op-amp #10: OA10 t1 (613,496), LEFT plate of cap #9, RIGHT lead of resistor #12.
  n8  = output node of op-amp #10: OA10 out (723,518), RIGHT plate of cap #9, LEFT lead of resistor #13.
  n9  = summing node (in-) of op-amp #14: OA14 t1 (236,613), LEFT lead of inductor #11, TOP terminal of I-DC #16.
  n10 = summing node (in-) of op-amp #20: OA20 t1 (590,817), LEFT lead of inductor #18, RIGHT plate of cap #21.
  n11 = output node of op-amp #20: OA20 out (723,841), RIGHT lead of inductor #18, LEFT lead of resistor #22.

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS (all eight recorded explicitly; every one agrees with the tracer default, but each was inspected):
  S4  (600,205) deg=3 - JUNCTION. A clean T: the x~600 drop from the 1uH feedback inductor ENDS on the y~205 rail, with a pen blob at the tee (dot=1.8). No crossing to interpret. Reading it any other way would strand the inductor's left lead.
  S10 (752,234) deg=5 - JUNCTION. Op-amp #3's output apex, the x~752 riser to the feedback inductor, and the wire on to resistor #6 all meet here. A crossing reading would sever the inductor feedback and leave the output driving only R#6; the riser visibly terminates at the rail.
  S23 (596,496) deg=3 - JUNCTION. T: the drop from cap #9's left plate ends on the wire running from resistor #12 to op-amp #10's in-. Not a crossing (nothing continues below).
  S24 (439,500) deg=4 - JUNCTION. This is the one genuine four-way decision on the sheet. inkmap at (439,500) shows the 3px vertical swelling to 8px (x 436-444) over y 491-503 exactly at the rail - a deliberate ink blob ~2.7x stroke width, i.e. a solder dot - and there is no hop and no sideways jog. Both readings are electrically sane, so the ink prior (plain crossing = junction in this dataset) plus the dot settle it. THE OTHER READING would split n5 into {inductor#11 right, R#12 left, OA#14 out} and {OA#3 in+, cap#21 left plate}, i.e. op-amp #14's output would drive only R#12 and op-amp #3's in+ would be fed only by cap #21 - 13 nets instead of 12. Rejected on the dot.
  S27 (377,500) deg=3 - JUNCTION. T with a blob: op-amp #14's output riser ends on the y~500 rail.
  S29 (744,517) deg=3 - JUNCTION. T: op-amp #10's output, the drop from cap #9's right plate, and the wire on to resistor #13 meet. A crossing would kill the cap #9 feedback.
  S30 (986,522) deg=3 - JUNCTION. T: resistor #13's right lead ends on the vertical output bus, which passes top-to-bottom. Not a crossing (nothing continues to the right of the bus).
  S38 (164,615) deg=3 - JUNCTION. T: the drop from inductor #11's left lead ends on the y~613 rail that carries the I-DC top terminal to op-amp #14's in-. A crossing would leave the inductor feedback open.
  Non-critical sites left at default, all verified to be handwriting or symbol ink brushing a wire and none change the netlist: S1/S19/S20/S22 ('1uH' labels), S9/S11/S12/S32 ('1kOhm' labels), S14 ('5V' label on the source circle), S16/S17 ('1uF' label), S3/S28 (drawn corners), S6 (a small drawn 'o' on the wire between OA#3's output and resistor #6), S7 (resistor #6's right lead meeting the bus), S36/S37 (same corner cluster as S38), S41/S42 (op-amp #20's input and output tees).

PIN-ORDER FIXES (all five op-amps were wrong): the drafter drew the '+' mark on the LOWER input of every triangle, and in each case that lower lead runs to a GND symbol while the upper lead carries the negative-feedback element. The tracer had assigned t0 to whichever lead it found first, which was the upper one on #2, #3, #10, #14 and #20. Corrected so that t0=in+ (lower, grounded), t1=in- (upper, feedback), t2=out:
  #2  ports {0:p1, 1:p0}   (p1@(280,232) lower = in+, p0@(279,192) upper = in-)
  #3  ports {0:p0, 1:p1}   (p0@(642,253) lower = in+, p1@(641,205) upper = in-)
  #10 ports {0:p2, 1:p1, 2:p0}  (p2@(613,539) lower = in+, p1@(613,496) upper = in-, p0@(723,518) out)
  #14 ports {0:p2, 1:p1, 2:p0}  (p2@(236,645) lower = in+, p1@(236,613) upper = in-, p0@(321,614) out)
  #20 ports {0:p0, 1:p2, 2:p1}  (p0@(590,867) lower = in+, p2@(590,817) upper = in-, p1@(723,841) out)

TERMINALS THAT LANDED ON HANDWRITING (fixed):
  #5 V-DC t1 was sitting on port p0@(109,279), which is a stroke of the '5V' value label brushing the source circle (see site S14) - net n8 had one terminal. Repointed to p3@(71,308), the real bottom lead, which runs down to GND #8. Now t1=0.
  #4 Resistor (top 1k) t0 was sitting on port p1@(489,227), which is the '1' glyph of its own '1KOhm' label (see sites S9/S11/S12) - net n6 had one terminal. There is no port on the real left lead because the annotated box swallows the whole zigzag (its leftmost ink is x=483, inside the box at x>=475), so `ports` cannot reach it and it is set with manual_nets.

BROKEN/FADED WIRES REPAIRED (both verified in the pixels, both are pencil lines that faded in the scan, not drafter intent):
  (a) y~197 rail between V-DC #5 and op-amp #2's in-: inkmap/zoom at (150,197) shows a continuous but progressively fainter line from the corner at x=62 to x~140, a break at x=143-150, a grey remnant at x=150-160, another break, then solid ink from x=173 to the corner at x=186 and on to the op-amp. The drafter plainly drew one wire. Repaired with merge [5.0, 2.1] -> net n4. Without it the source's top terminal and the op-amp's inverting input are two one-terminal nets, i.e. the 5V source drives nothing.
  (b) top rail between the corner at (185,93) and cap #0's LEFT plate at x=290: inkmap at (256,92) shows ink to x=227, then paper, then a surviving dash at x=276-281 y=94, then the plate. Same faded-pencil signature. Cap #0's left terminal has no port at all (the tracer found only one port on that box), so it is asserted with manual_nets 0.0 = n4 - the net the y~93 rail belongs to. Without it the feedback capacitor of stage 1 has a floating plate and the y~93 rail is a dead-end stub.
  (c) y~208 run between op-amp #2's output blob at (414,210) and resistor #4's left end at x=483: inkmap at (448,210) shows solid ink to x=421, an isolated horizontal dash at x=439-445 y=209-211 lying exactly on the straight line between the two ends (no handwriting anywhere near that spot - the '1KOhm' text is at y 225-270), then paper to x=482 where the zigzag starts. Asserted with manual_nets 4.0 = n1. Without it op-amp #2's output feeds nothing but its own feedback capacitor and the 1k resistor's left end dangles - the entire first stage would be dead, which is not what is drawn.

CLASSES: no corrections. Every symbol matches its label (5 Op-Amp #2 #3 #10 #14 #20, 5 Resistor #4 #6 #12 #13 #22, 3 Capacitor #0 #9 #21, 3 Inductor #1 #11 #18, 1 V-DC, 1 I-DC, 6 GND). Nothing looked mis-classified.

UNRESOLVED / RESIDUAL DOUBT: the only place I am relying on inference rather than unbroken ink is the three faded runs (a)/(b)/(c) above; in each case there is surviving ink on the intended path and the alternative leaves a component terminal or a source floating, so I am confident, but they are flagged here for audit. Net n6 (the x~986 bus) is a three-resistor node with no other load - that is what is drawn; it is not an error.
